hints: Focus on what is the same and what is different here, since all three species have 10 electrons but different nuclear charges.
Count the protons in each species: F has 9, Ne has 10, and Na has 11, so think about which nucleus pulls those 10 electrons in most strongly.
Remember that greater proton number means greater attraction and a smaller radius, so arrange them from strongest pull (smallest) to weakest pull (largest).
walkthrough:
**Spot the isoelectronic set**

Great start, let's see what we have. All three species have the same electron arrangement, 10 electrons each, like neon.

$\text{F}^- : 9 \text{ protons, } 10 \text{ electrons}$ , $\text{Ne} : 10 \text{ protons, } 10 \text{ electrons}$ , $\text{Na}^+ : 11 \text{ protons, } 10 \text{ electrons}$

**Apply the key idea: nuclear charge wins**

When electrons are the same, size is decided by how hard the nucleus pulls. More protons means a stronger pull, drawing the same electron cloud in closer.

Pulling power: $\text{Na}^+ (11+) > \text{Ne} (10+) > \text{F}^- (9+)$

**Order from smallest to largest**

Strongest pull gives the smallest radius, weakest pull gives the largest radius. So the order of increasing radius is the reverse of proton number.

smallest $\text{Na}^+$ < $\text{Ne}$ < $\text{F}^-$ largest

options.A: Starts correctly with Na+ as smallest, but then puts F- before Ne. F- has only 9 protons pulling on 10 electrons, so electron repulsion wins and it is larger than Ne, not smaller.
options.B: Puts F- smallest and Na+ largest, which is exactly backwards. This is the trap of thinking more electrons or a negative charge always means smaller, or confusing ionic charge with nuclear charge.
options.C: Correct. With 10 electrons each, the 11 protons of Na+ pull hardest giving the smallest radius, Ne is in the middle, and the 9 protons of F- pull weakest giving the largest radius.
options.D: Puts Ne smallest and Na+ largest. This ignores nuclear charge. Na+ has the most protons (11) for the same electrons, so it must be smallest, not largest.
